analysis.analysis: The Overview composes the database at the grain of its own about page and keeps it apart from its neighbours. It gives the operator, the model and the derived layer, and omits the incident-and-report structure that makes the database what it is. This is the baseline for the meta-aggregator's record, which was not yet indexed: no card is machinemediation.org.
analysis.d: THE AI INCIDENT DATABASE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a free, open-source project managed by the Responsible AI Collaborative that indexes real-world harms, near-harms, and failures caused by artificial intelligence systems'. Four points: the aviation and cybersecurity reporting model, a scope of harms (bias, privacy, misinformation, deepfakes, vehicles, safety-critical failures), growth with deepfake and scam entries multiplying, and the MIT AI Incident Tracker as a research extension that parses the database with taxonomies and LLM pipelines. Six cards: the database, the MIT tracker, Partnership on AI, the OECD catalogue entry, a Kaggle dataset, a TIME clip.
analysis.d_full: THE AI INCIDENT DATABASE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a free, open-source project managed by the Responsible AI Collaborative that indexes real-world harms, near-harms, and failures caused by artificial intelligence systems'. Four points: the aviation and cybersecurity reporting model, a scope of harms (bias, privacy, misinformation, deepfakes, vehicles, safety-critical failures), growth with deepfake and scam entries multiplying, and the MIT AI Incident Tracker as a research extension that parses the database with taxonomies and LLM pipelines. Six cards: the database, the MIT tracker, Partnership on AI, the OECD catalogue entry, a Kaggle dataset, a TIME clip.
findings: THE ENTITY HELD. Operator (the Responsible AI Collaborative), purpose ('harms, near-harms'), the aviation model and the MIT tracker as a derived layer are the record's fields: the about page's operator, the comparison with aviation on its home and about pages, and the tracker's own statement that it classifies AIID reports with Arcola AI's pipeline. Checked 2026-10-29 against the MMRS meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 and the entity's own pages, re-read the same day.
WHAT IS NOT GIVEN. The incident as the unit, the reports attached to it, and the citation page /cite/N are absent; 'collects public and crowdsourced reports' stands in for the unit.

A HOMONYM IN THE CARDS. 'AI Incidents, Failures & Controversies Database' on Kaggle (32 incidents, 29 companies, 13 countries) is another dataset with a near name; the composition does not use it, and the card sits beside the database's own.
'OPEN-SOURCE'. The database's code is open on GitHub (its about page); the record states no data licence on the snapshots page, and the composition's 'free, open-source' does not distinguish the two.

[QUERENT] ai incident database

[SYSTEM] The [AI Incident Database](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVhCp3r30WDl_s74Tm7Hc1aBx4m9gUEfwR4rqNmGz-8J-kaBBPEf7oCzpPsVYpI0IjKz6xRnV6Cp3Gh2ovoUhN7Tqyc-CNOsFltlelT6uSJw) is a free, open-source project managed by the [Responsible AI Collaborative](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVQJB-mdnnQ6r52BIfaBkZdpvIYmeG5iTBUzeQEwySxYcKr4WzFleLjuPKMrQKQTK3W2B9l2jGnS5pLy19F1B1fTurJ-XoVDm2xfief4Gqb_ptw2t6ueReQR1dw3n-38GlP31Dx2C5MCLIXg) that indexes real-world harms, near-harms, and failures caused by artificial intelligence systems. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVhCp3r30WDl_s74Tm7Hc1aBx4m9gUEfwR4rqNmGz-8J-kaBBPEf7oCzpPsVYpI0IjKz6xRnV6Cp3Gh2ovoUhN7Tqyc-CNOsFltlelT6uSJw), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVQJB-mdnnQ6r52BIfaBkZdpvIYmeG5iTBUzeQEwySxYcKr4WzFleLjuPKMrQKQTK3W2B9l2jGnS5pLy19F1B1fTurJ-XoVDm2xfief4Gqb_ptw2t6ueReQR1dw3n-38GlP31Dx2C5MCLIXg)]

* Aviation Safety Model: Modeled after safety incident reporting systems used in aviation and cybersecurity, it collects public and crowdsourced reports to help the industry learn from past failures.
